intent: monitor room concept generation and targeted refinement

images.prompt:
Redesign the monitoring/security control room shown inside the RED RECTANGLE of reference image 1, and produce one polished final in-game room concept, enlarged to fill the canvas.
Image 1 is the campus master-plan reference: faithfully retain its compact security-room identity, northern wall covered by TWO ROWS OF FOUR surveillance screens, control console directly below, a tall equipment rack along the right side, restrained filing and logbook furniture. Image 2 is the current Godot map-editor reference: match its orthographic overhead 2D hand-painted game camera, straight horizontal and vertical world axes, visible vertical front faces, and illustrated outlines. Do NOT reproduce the editor interface or the whole campus.
Camera and composition: a single roof-removed cutaway room, almost square interior with width to length ratio 380:420. Entire room and south entrance visible with a narrow paved exterior margin. Northern back wall at top, south doorway at bottom center. No diagonal isometric axes, no perspective room photography. Crisp readable actual game-ready painted sprites with restrained realistic texture, like existing game furniture. Source references are low-resolution but output must have clean detailed edges, no blur or sandy noisy filter.
Architectural identity: an aged factory-era security control room. Light cool gray plaster above muted slate blue-gray painted metal wainscot panels, dark charcoal base molding, thin squared steel corner posts with clean continuous joins. Lower walls at left/right and cutaway south front. Neutral pale gray-green small square floor tiles with sparse wear. A compact closed blue-gray security door at SOUTH CENTER, about 40% of the room width, key lock/access box beside its right jamb, tiny restrained red indicator. A small physical plaque above the entrance bears ONLY the Chinese text “监控室”. No large floor title. No cream industrial thick rounded wall caps, no hospital green tiles, no wooden noticeboard dominating the north wall.
Furniture composition: eight old thick-bezel blue/gray CRT security monitors in a 4-by-2 grid, mounted against the upper north wall spanning the LEFT 70% of room width. Screens show tiny dim grayscale-blue views of corridor, yard, and loading area, some scanlines, one dark screen; low-intensity screen light only, no neon blue room lighting. A matching charcoal/slate metal console directly underneath with small keyboard, pushbuttons, telephone/intercom and a few controlled status lights, height and depth scaled to a single human operator. Keep screen wall and console coherent but visibly distinct layers. One simple worn dark operator chair centered in front of console. To the RIGHT of monitors, one slim floor-standing equipment cabinet with vents, recorder decks, tapes and very small amber/green LEDs, against east wall; front accessible. Lower-left side: one low metal filing cabinet with a few folders on top and a SMALL wall clipboard above. Lower-right side: one compact brown logbook desk with an open register, pencil and a desk lamp, oriented horizontally, tucked to east wall. Minimal visible cables in tidy trunking along the wall. No many duplicated cabinets, no loot icons, no crates, no giant futuristic sci-fi screens.
Human scale: one short illustrated uniformed guard in dark blue shirt and cap stands in the open center-left area next to the operator chair, as a size reference. Keep this game's slightly cartoon character proportions, full body about 84 world units high, so the 380-wide room fits around 4.5 character heights. Use exactly ONE guard, no medical character. Screens, console and chair must feel usable at this scale.
Movement: leave an unmistakable clear central walkway from south door to chair and console, about 100–120 world units wide, no furniture in the doorway, space in front of recorder cabinet and desk. Furnishings concentrated near walls, center functional and compact, not a large empty hall.
Color/material: low-saturation slate blue-gray metal, pale gray-green floor, charcoal monitors, dull brown desk, subtle cream paper; sparse rust/wear at hinges and corners. Warm neutral ambient light, contact shadows uniformly down-right. Main focal point is the 8-screen monitor wall. Design remains appropriate for the industrial prison campus.
Output: ONE full-color final environment concept art image. Entire cutaway room at large scale, quiet exterior pavement margin only. No multi-panel presentation board, no furniture callout diagrams, no annotations, no arrows, no red reference rectangles, no decorative border, no game HUD, no title at top.

Refine image 1, the supplied monitoring room final concept. Preserve its exact room proportions, overhead orthographic camera, tiled floor, eight CRT screens in two rows of four, their images, console, recorder rack, chair, filing cabinet, logbook desk, doorway location and Chinese plaque “监控室”. Keep the same crisp hand-painted industrial prison game environment.
Change only TWO details:
1. Replace the thick creamy beige stone cap around the room with a NARROW, clean, squared slate BLUE-GRAY painted steel edge/coping, subtle seams and small rivets. It should look like a dedicated security office construction, match the dark blue-gray wainscot and steel door, and have continuous tightly joined right-angle corners. No beige cream rounded industrial wall cap. Upper wall plaster remains light cool gray, lower panels blue-gray, lighting unchanged. Make the perimeter border visually about half its current thickness while retaining the same overall floor and furniture layout.
2. Replace the ONE realistic proportioned guard with ONE existing-game CARTOON guard based on the LEFT idle pose in reference image 2: large head and cap, short compact body, navy uniform, simple black outlines, round nose, small black boots, exactly the game's hand-painted sprite character proportions. Face slightly to screen right. Keep his current location and total height on screen so furniture size remains consistent. Reference image 2 is a character sheet only, use just a single idle guard, do not include multiple guards or a sprite sheet.
Do not change or add any other furniture, monitors, objects, labels or room lights. No UI, annotations, border, glow or extra people. One polished enlarged room final concept image.
